It depends on what limits the backlog. Reminder jobs are mostly I/O, so higher concurrency per process is cheap if CPU is low, but it's capped by the email provider's rate limits and DB connections, while more replicas multiply the same connection use. I don't have the numbers yet.
Action: Check worker CPU and memory, average job duration, queue depth and the email provider's limits, then recommend; I'd likely try a modest concurrency bump first if CPU has headroom.
